rule: logical = at least one example task's answer changed. noise = at least one touched example, all touched examples unchanged, no prior change that moved an outcome. ambiguous = no example shows a change and no touched example proves nothing changed, or the evidence is mixed (for example touched and unchanged examples but a prior similar change that moved an outcome, or conflicting priors, or only one thin untouched example).

H2-N1.why: Playlist order changes, but the checker ignores order. Both touched examples keep the same answer.

H2-N2.why: Venmo amounts gain a dollar sign, but the checker strips it. Both touched examples keep the same answer.

H2-L1.why: Times switch from local to UTC. The 9am meeting example flips from solved to NOT solved.

H2-L2.why: Contacts with the same name must now all be listed. The Alex example flips from solved to NOT solved.

H2-N3.why: Email subjects are lower cased, but the checker lower cases both sides. Both touched examples keep the same answer. The prior is noise from the H2-N1 run.

H2-L3.why: The text says wording cleanup, but a money answer must now include the currency symbol. The $80 example flips from solved to NOT solved. The noise prior is misleading.

H2-A1.why: Weights may switch to pounds, but the only example is a count, not a weight, and untouched. Thin evidence, proves nothing either way.

H2-A2.why: Phone formatting may change, but both examples are names and email, untouched. The priors conflict, one noise and one logical, both from real earlier runs in this test.

H2-A3.why: Only Venmo changes, Amazon does not. The Venmo example is touched and unchanged, the Amazon example is untouched. Partial coverage, proves nothing about Venmo amounts.

H2-A4.why: Two touched examples are unchanged, which points to noise, but a prior similar time change, H2-L1, moved an outcome. Mixed evidence, so hold.
